New Floodplain Maps Take Effect This November in Larimer County

2026-08-24 Larimer County Engineering floodplain maps, FEMA, Flood Insurance Rate Maps, FIRM, Larimer County, Colorado, flood risk, NFIP, hydrology, topography
Read the source article

Quick summary

Larimer County, Colorado's updated Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs) become effective November 27, 2026, incorporating new topography and hydrology data following the September 2013 flood, requiring county adoption to remain in the National Flood Insurance Program.

Key takeaways

  • Updated Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs) and Flood Insurance Study (FIS) become effective November 27, 2026
  • The update is a response to the September 2013 flood and represents a proactive effort to update flood risks
  • New topography and hydrology data have been incorporated into the updated floodplain maps
  • Larimer County must adopt the updated FIRMs and FIS to remain in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)
  • Property owners can check if their property is affected via the county's online resources
  • Public hearing dates are available for residents to learn about flood insurance impacts
  • The maps affect Unincorporated Larimer County specifically
